name: LP8868XQDMTRQ1
title: Automotive 65 V multi-topology LED driver with integrated switch and inductive fast dimming
summary: LP8868-Q1 is an AEC-Q100 grade 1 single-string LED driver with a built-in 150 mΩ low-side switch, run as a non-synchronous boost (LP8868X/U), buck-boost (LP8868Y/V) or buck (LP8868Z/W) from 4.5 V to 65 V. It switches at 100 kHz to 2.2 MHz, optionally with spread spectrum, and regulates LED current from a 200 mV sense threshold with adaptive off-time current-mode control. Analog, PWM, hybrid and flexible dimming are chosen by the levels on ADIM/HD and EN/PWM. LED open and short, sense-resistor faults, switch faults and thermal shutdown are flagged on FAULT; a thermal foldback curve is set by one resistor.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 65 V (recommended 4.5 V to 63 V)
VSON-14 4.5 mm × 3 mm; HVSSOP-12 4 mm × 4.9 mm

notes: Each VSON part number also orders with a .A suffix.

circuits.title: LP8868X boost driver, 12 V input, 8 LEDs at 1 A
circuits.description: Boost converter from a 9 V to 16 V rail. L1 runs from the input to SW; D1 carries the switched current out through RSENSE to the top of a string of eight LEDs whose bottom end is ground. RSENSE (200 mΩ) with CSENSE across it sits between the diode and the output, so CSP sees the diode side and CSN, through 100 Ω, the output side; 1 nF ties CSP to CSN at the pins. ROVP1/ROVP2 divide the output down to OVP for the LED-open threshold. RCOMP in series with CCOMP, shunted by RDAMP, compensates COMP. RFSET and RTEMP to ground set frequency and foldback, both dimming inputs take PWM signals, and FAULT is pulled up to VCC.

parts.note: X7R ceramic at the VIN pin
across CSP and CSN at the pins

notes: With 10 µH the inductor ripple, peak and rms currents come to 1.41 A, 3.67 A and 2.96 A; the boost inductor equation gives 11.9 µH for VIN(min) = 9 V, VOUT = 24 V, ILED = 1 A, efficiency 0.9, IL(max) = 2.96 A, KIND = 0.4.
Input capacitors chosen: 33 µF 100 V electrolytic, 10 µF 100 V X7R and 0.1 µF 100 V X7R; input ripple about 88 mV.
RSENSE dissipates 200 mW at 1 A.
Sense-feedback high-frequency filter: 0.1 µF, 50 V X7R.
The switching current limit of 5.8 A bounds the output current.

circuits.title: LP8868Y buck-boost driver, 12 V input, 5 LEDs at 1 A
circuits.description: Buck-boost from a 9 V to 16 V rail with the LED string returned to the input: L1 from the input to SW, D1 from SW through RSENSE to the output node, and five LEDs from the output node back up to VIN. COUT and the ROVP1/ROVP2 divider go from the output node to ground, the divider tap feeding OVP. Current sense, compensation, FSET, TEMP, dimming and FAULT connect as in the boost circuit.

circuits.title: LP8868Z buck driver, 12 V input, 1 LED at 2 A
circuits.description: Low-side buck from a 9 V to 16 V rail. The LED anode sits on VIN; its cathode goes through RSENSE (100 mΩ) and L1 to SW, and D1 returns the inductor current from SW to VIN. COUT is across the LED. CSP takes the LED-cathode end of RSENSE and CSN, through 100 Ω, the inductor end, with 1 nF between the pins. RUVP1/RUVP2 divide the LED cathode down to UVP. Compensation, FSET, TEMP, dimming and FAULT connect as in the boost circuit; a capacitor across RSENSE is optional in buck and none is fitted.

operation.text: LP8868X and LP8868U are boost parts, LP8868Y and LP8868V buck-boost, LP8868Z and LP8868W buck. X, Y and Z have spread spectrum on; U, V and W have it off. All integrate the low-side N-channel switch (150 mΩ typ) and use an external Schottky diode; the converter is non-synchronous. Supported input range 4.5 V to 65 V. The family supports a common-cathode LED connection and single-layer boards.

Adaptive off-time current-mode control. The error amplifier compares the voltage across the sense resistor (CSP to CSN) with VREF; its output, VCOMP, goes through the external compensation network to the PWM comparator. The internal FET doubles as the peak-current sensor; once that peak reaches VCOMP the FET turns off and an off-time counter runs. The off time follows the FSET resistor and an input/output feed-forward, which keeps the frequency close to constant in steady state while regulating the average LED current.
Set from 100 kHz to 2.2 MHz by RFSET from FSET to AGND (59 kΩ gives 400 kHz); an open FSET gives 100 kHz. A lower frequency generally gives better efficiency and thermal behaviour.

LP8868X/Y/Z dither the switching frequency ±7 % about the centre at a 2 kHz modulation rate to lower EMI at the fundamental and harmonics. LP8868U/V/W run without it, which favours low-brightness performance.

RSENSE between CSP and CSN sets the LED current against VREF = 200 mV. A capacitor across RSENSE is required in boost and buck-boost for inductive fast dimming (IFD) and low-duty accuracy, and is optional in buck. A 100 Ω resistor in series with CSN is recommended against noise pickup.

Once VIN passes VVIN_MIN the LDO charges the VCC capacitor; with 1 µF, VCC takes about 800 µs to pass VVIN_UVLO. If EN/PWM is already high, power-on reset follows directly and dimming starts 100 µs later; EN/PWM must stay high for more than 5 µs after VCC crosses VVIN_UVLO. With 1 µF on VCC, allow 1 ms after VIN passes VVIN_MIN before dimming begins. If the first EN/PWM pulse arrives after VCC is up, POR waits 200 µs and dimming a further 100 µs, so a re-enable without a VIN UVLO takes 300 µs. The first enable pulse must be longer than 5 µs. Once dimming starts, the device runs in the mode set by ADIM/HD and EN/PWM.

ADIM/HD held high, PWM on EN/PWM. A rising edge starts switching and the inductor current ramps to the regulated level, held while the input is high; a falling edge turns the FET off and the current falls to zero. Input pulses down to 200 ns are supported in this mode. In hybrid dimming a reversal of the duty-cycle direction is acted on only when the duty changes by more than 0.38 %.

EN/PWM held high, PWM on ADIM/HD. VREF scales with the ADIM duty cycle (200 mV at 100 %, 20 mV at 10 %); the internal logic follows a duty change within a few tens of microseconds. Dimming ratio 256:1.

ADIM/HD held low, PWM on EN/PWM. From 12.5 % to 100 % brightness VREF scales with the EN/PWM duty (analog); below 12.5 % VREF stays fixed and an internal PWM generator, with frequency and duty taken from the EN/PWM input, switches the LEDs on and off.
PWM signals on both pins: EN/PWM switches the LEDs on and off, while the ADIM/HD duty sets VREF, so current level and on/off timing are independent.

The UVLO watches VCC: the device turns off when VCC falls below about 3.0 V, with about 0.2 V hysteresis. VCC is regulated from VIN, so UVLO trips once VIN comes within roughly 500 mV of that threshold.
An open LED string, an LED node shorted to ground, an open or shorted sense resistor, a failed switching FET, thermal shutdown and VIN UVLO each pull FAULT low.

Above Tth, set by RTEMP from TEMP to GND (80 °C to 150 °C; 130 °C with 20 kΩ), the full-scale current IFS drops by about 2 % per °C until it reaches 50 %, i.e. 25 °C above Tth, then keeps falling more slowly up to the thermal shutdown threshold TTSD. Mounting the device and LEDs on a shared thermal substrate helps.
Input 4.5 V to 65 V from a well-regulated source, with an X5R or X7R ceramic input capacitor; 10 µF suits most designs.

Large GND plane; wide IN and GND traces; thermal vias from the top GND copper to inner layers; input capacitors next to the IN and GND pins; VCC capacitor next to VCC; SW trace as short as possible; no switching current under the device; CSP and CSN routed as a short parallel pair away from the switching trace; compensation capacitor next to COMP.
